# Executive Summary

Across **Chapter 3** (isogenic LOY model engineering and multi-omic characterization) and **Chapter 4** (public pharmacogenomic/CRISPR power analyses, genome-wide isogenic Brunello CRISPR screens, and reciprocal spectral flow-cytometry competition assays), we establish a complete framework connecting chromosome Y structure, lineage-dependent versus conserved transcriptional and chromatin remodelling, *UTY*-mediated transcriptional reversibility, and paralog versus coactivator/metabolic synthetic lethal dependencies.

---

# Module-by-Module Headline Findings

## §1 Public DepMap CRISPR & PRISM Drug Screens (`01_depmap_prism_public/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 4, §4.3.0 (`Fig 4.1`, `Supp Fig 4.1–4.4`).
- **Y-status classification & core gametolog recovery:** Across **568 classified male DepMap CRISPR models** (404 Y-retaining, 164 LOY), pan-cancer linear models and Random Forest / Boruta feature selection recover four established X-linked paralog dependencies selectively required in LOY lines: ***DDX3X***, ***EIF1AX***, ***RPS4X***, and ***ZFX***.
- **Replication in 3D malignant organoid and neurosphere cohorts:** Across Sanger Project Score and **DepMap NextGen 3D organoid/neurosphere screens**, ***DDX3X***, ***EIF1AX***, and ***RPS4X*** meet the permutation-based replication criteria, whereas *ZFX* does not replicate in NextGen 3D models (`Fig 4.1f`).
- **Context-stratified genetic searches & empirical power limits:** Across lineage/disease subsets, **86 driver/genomic alteration contexts** (523,654 interaction tests), and **24 cancer-type $\times$ driver combinations** (146,136 interaction tests; 414,052 within-subset tests), no additional non-gametolog genetic dependency passes strict family-wise FDR control (`Supp Fig 4.2`). Transferring **25 benchmark synthetic lethalities** (e.g., *WRN*–MSI, *PRMT5*–*MTAP*, *KRAS*, *BRAF*) onto observed LOY sample splits via empirical power simulations demonstrates that once public cohorts are subdivided by lineage or driver mutation, sample sizes and inter-line variance prevent detection of even benchmark-strength vulnerabilities in most subsets (`Supp Fig 4.3`).
- **Pharmacological screens:** Across **6,413 pan-cancer drug comparisons** (PRISM Repurposing Primary/Secondary, PRISM REP.1M, GDSC1/2, CTD2) and **495,079 finite within-subset drug tests** across 121 binary contexts, positive controls recover expected target sensitivities, but no pan-cancer LOY drug sensitivity reaches significance (`Supp Fig 4.4`; one within-subset association at $\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$ is lower sensitivity to `SR-1664` in LOY mature B-cell neoplasms in PRISM REP.1M, $\Delta = +0.667$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.031$).

## §2 Repeat-Targeting Guide Design, ddPCR & lpWGS (`02_genome_engineering/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 3, §3.3.1–3.3.2 (`Fig 3.1–3.6`, `Supp Fig 3.4–3.14`).
- **T2T-Y repeat guide discovery:** Sliding-window scanning of the complete `T2T-CHM13v2.0` (HG002) Y assembly yielded **14,723 candidate 20-nt NGG guides**, filtered to **6,901 guides** with zero exact non-Y matches and **215 high-copy top hits** (`Supp Fig 3.4`). Five lead guides were characterized across three repeat arrays (`Fig 3.1`): centromeric `DYZ3` $\alpha$-satellite (`CP` [35 exact T2T-Y sites], `CN` [35 sites]), `Yq12` `DYZ1`/`HSat3` (`Q53` [259 sites]), and `Yp` *TSPY* (`P47` [46 sites], `P51` [34 sites]).
- **Pooled RNP engineering & multiplex ddPCR:** Delivering `CP + Q53` Cas9 RNPs transiently across two successive nucleofections (`2x`) achieves **88–99% depletion of Yq target copies** directly in bulk pooled populations of HT1080 fibrosarcoma and A549 lung adenocarcinoma cells without single-cell cloning (`Fig 3.2`). Notably, `CP` outperforms `CN` despite identical reference repeat counts in the same `DYZ3` array. In DU145, pre-treating cells with the pan-HDAC inhibitor **panobinostat** (30–75 nM for 24 h before nucleofection) substantially enhances single-round Y depletion compared with DMSO or post-nucleofection ATM inhibition with `KU-55933` (`Supp Fig 3.13`).
- **Y-PAR-masked T2T-Y lpWGS & partial distal Yp retention:** Combining 100-kb `QDNAseq`/`mosdepth` copy-number profiling on a Y-PAR-masked `T2T-CHM13v2.0` reference with regional RNA-seq across HT1080 (`Fig 3.3–3.4`), A549 (`Fig 3.5`), and DU145 (`Fig 3.6`) reveals distinct structural outcomes:
  - **A549 (`CP + Q53 2x`):** Near-complete loss across the entire Y chromosome (`Yp` and `Yq` median DNA retention ~10–12%; MSY expression depleted across both arms).
  - **HT1080 (`CP + Q53 2x`):** Complete loss of euchromatic `Yq` (<1% expression from *USP9Y* to *EIF1AY*) and strong proximal `Yp` depletion, but residual retention of distal male-specific `Yp` (~20–36% expression of *RPS4Y1* and *ZFY*).
  - **DU145 (`CP + Q53 + P47 2x`, historically mislabelled "LNCaP" and verified as DU145 via STR and transcriptomic lineage profiling):** Complete loss of euchromatic `Yq` and 96–98% depletion at proximal `Yp` (*AMELY* at ~6.5 Mb), but **46–54% DNA and RNA retention across a distal male-specific `Yp` segment (~2.46–4.80 Mb)** containing *RPS4Y1* and *ZFY* (`Fig 3.6`, `Supp Fig 3.11–3.12`).

## §3 Bulk RNA-Seq & Comparative Transcriptomics (`03_rnaseq_transcriptomics/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 3, §3.3.3 (`Fig 3.7–3.8`, `Fig 3.11–3.13`, `Supp Fig 3.1–3.2`, `Supp Fig 3.15–3.20`, `Supp Fig 3.29–3.41`).
- **HT1080 baseline RNA-seq (`SEPT_11_2026_REANALYZE`):** Across 12 core libraries spanning two sampling windows (August 2025 & May 2026; 25,526 expressed autosomal/non-PAR X genes) plus 3 parental libraries, Y depletion drives **1,003 high-confidence non-Y/non-PAR DEGs** ($\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$, $|\log_2\mathrm{FC}| \ge 1$, concordant direction in both windows: 551 higher, 452 lower; `Fig 3.7`). `PAR1` retains 68.8%/66.8% and `PAR2` retains 60.2%/63.6% of `sgCTRL` expression. Pathway (`fgsea` and fixed-correlation `CAMERA`, $\rho = 0.01$) and 42 STRING protein-association modules (`Fig 3.8`, `Supp Fig 3.16–3.20`) reveal strong suppression of **type I/II interferon, inflammatory/cytokine, and ECM/contractile programmes** alongside upregulation of **neural/synaptic adhesion (*UNC5A*, *SDK2*, *ROR2*) and cholesterol/sterol biosynthesis**.
- **A549 baseline RNA-seq (`SEPT_18_2026_REANALYZE`):** Using the primary `RINe`-adjusted `limma-voom` model across 22,843 expressed nuclear genes, Y depletion yields **27 $\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$ genes**: 17 MSY genes and only **10 non-Y/non-PAR genes** (8 higher, 2 lower; `Supp Fig 3.29–3.30`), with trend-level suppression of interferon/inflammatory gene sets.
- **DU145 baseline RNA-seq (`SEPT_23_2026_REANALYZE`):** Across 6 passage-matched libraries (`P12`–`P14`, paired `~ passage + treatment`), Y depletion identifies **136 non-Y/non-PAR DEGs at $\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$** and **114 passage-consistent genes** ($\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$, $|\log_2\mathrm{FC}| \ge 0.5$, 3/3 passage pairs agreeing: 83 lower, 31 higher; `Fig 3.11`). Copy-number-independent transcriptional changes feature pronounced suppression of the epithelial identity factor ***GRHL2*** and luminal/interferon programmes alongside induction of basement-membrane collagens and ECM remodelling without canonical EMT transcription-factor activation (`Fig 3.12`, `Supp Fig 3.32–3.39`).
- **Cross-cell-line & 18 external Y-loss comparisons (`crossline_SEPT_2026`):** All three engineered models exhibit **zero compensatory upregulation of X-linked gametologs** (`Fig 3.13a,b`). Pairwise autosomal gene-level correlations between HT1080, A549, and DU145 are near zero ($\rho = -0.06$ to $0.11$), yet pathway enrichment converges on **suppressed interferon-$\alpha$/$\gamma$ and inflammatory responses** across our models and 18 external Y-loss, naturally Y-mosaic single-cell (`GSE313572`, Tahoe-100M DMSO lines), MB49, 45,X, and *UTY*-KO datasets (`Fig 3.13c,d`, `Supp Fig 3.40`).
- **Comparison with 16 chromosome/arm-loss models (`arm_loss_bundle_2026-09-29`):** Benchmarking against acute RPTEC Yq vs. 3p loss (`GSE130306`), ReDACT trisomy corrections, and RPE1 monosomies shows that ribosomal-protein downregulation is a general feature of autosomal arm/chromosome loss, whereas interferon suppression and early-vs-late culture inversions distinguish specific karyotypic and temporal trajectories (`Supp Fig 3.41`).

## §4 Chromatin Accessibility & Multi-Omic Integration (`04_atacseq_chromatin/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 3, §3.3.3.1 (`Fig 3.9–3.10`, `Supp Fig 3.3`, `Supp Fig 3.21–3.28`).
- **Widespread chromatin compaction:** Across 6 HT1080 ATAC-seq libraries (`sgCTRL` and `LOY` at passages 11, 12, and 21; 105,647 consensus autosomal/non-PAR X peaks), Y depletion induces **758 differentially accessible regions (DARs) at $\mathrm{FDR} < 0.05$**, skewed **~7:1 toward chromatin closing** (**663 closed vs. 95 opened peaks**; `Fig 3.9`). Accessibility shifts are independent of autosomal DNA copy number ($\rho = -0.05$; `Supp Fig 3.23`).
- **Motif & footprinting landscape:** `chromVAR`, HOMER, and TOBIAS footprinting show decreased accessibility at **AP-1 (`FOS`/`JUN`), `CTF`/`NFIC`, and `IRF`** motifs in closing distal/promoter regions, and relative retention/enrichment of **GC-rich `KLF`/`SP`, `ETS`, and `Forkhead`** motifs (`Supp Fig 3.24–3.27`).
- **Concordant promoter closing & Polycomb target enrichment:** Downregulated HT1080 DEGs are **>30-fold more likely to exhibit promoter closing** than non-DE genes, and mean TSS accessibility drops by 21% even across downregulated genes lacking a discrete DAR call (`Fig 3.10`). Promoters that are jointly closed and transcriptionally repressed are significantly enriched for canonical **PRC2 (*EZH2*/*SUZ12*) and H3K27me3 targets** even after strict covariate matching on baseline accessibility, GC content, and CpG density (`Fig 3.10`, `Supp Fig 3.28`).

## §5 Lentiviral *UTY* and *KDM5D* Add-Back Rescue (`05_uty_kdm5d_addback/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 3, §3.3.4 (`Fig 3.14–3.15`, `Supp Fig 3.42–3.44`).
- **Design & construct verification:** 18 RNA-seq libraries across 6 HT1080 populations (`Parental`, `sgCTRL`, untransduced `LOY`, `LOY + Empty Vector`, `LOY + UTY`, `LOY + KDM5D`, and descendant `LOY + UTY + KDM5D` across 3 matched collection occasions) confirm robust transgene expression while non-transduced MSY genes remain absent (`Fig 3.14`).
- **Selective partial rescue by *UTY*:** Re-expressing ***UTY*** alone or in combination with *KDM5D* reverses **51.1%** ($P = 1.9 \times 10^{-4}$) and **35.1%** ($P = 0.0031$) of the independently derived 150-gene batch-1 HT1080 LOY signature (and significantly shifts the frozen-100-gene signature and directional `fry` tests), whereas ***KDM5D* expression alone produces no signature recovery** (`-5.5%`, $P = 0.65$; `Fig 3.15`, `Supp Fig 3.43`).
- **Recovery by baseline ATAC-seq promoter class:** *UTY* rescue preferentially re-induces baseline-downregulated genes whose promoters closed upon Y depletion (**36 of 39 joint RNA-down / ATAC-closed genes** shift upward in `LOY + UTY` vs. `LOY + EV`; `Supp Fig 3.43d`, `Supp Fig 3.44`).

## §6 Isogenic Genome-Wide Brunello CRISPR Screens (`06_crispr_screens/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 4, §4.3.1, §4.3.5, §4.3.6 (`Fig 4.2–4.4`, `Fig 4.7–4.8`, `Supp Fig 4.5–4.11`, `Supp Fig 4.13–4.16`).
- **HT1080 genome-wide Brunello screen:** Screening matched `sgCTRL` and `LOY` HT1080 populations (76,441 targeting guides + 1,000 NTCs; `D0`, `D12`, `D21`; primary unpaired `drugZ` plus `MAGeCK` and baseline-adjusted `IsogenicZ`) identifies ***DDX3X*** as the #1 genome-wide LOY synthetic lethal hit ($\mathrm{normZ} = -11.45$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 2.13 \times 10^{-26}$; `Fig 4.2–4.3`). Beyond *DDX3X*, the screen nominates coordinated vulnerabilities in:
  - **SAGA coactivator complex (6 of 20 subunits):** *TAF6L* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -4.87$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.0067$), *TADA2B* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -4.29$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.046$), *SUPT20H* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -4.19$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.056$), *ATXN7L3* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -3.91$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.125$), *TADA1* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -3.77$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.165$), and exploratory *TAF5L* (`Fig 4.3–4.4`).
  - **Mediator & chromatin regulators:** *MED12* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -5.06$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 0.0040$), X-linked *BCORL1*.
  - **Lipid, sterol & selenoprotein metabolism:** *SREBF2*, *SREBF1*, *SCLY*, *ACSL4*.
  - **Mitochondrial & adhesion factors:** X-linked *TIMM8A* ($\mathrm{normZ} = -5.73$, $\mathrm{FDR} = 2.02 \times 10^{-4}$), *LLGL1*, *ITGB5*.
- **A549 genome-wide Brunello screen & rules of gametolog recovery:** In A549 (`Fig 4.7–4.8`), endpoint and trimmed-`P3` `IsogenicZ` analyses recover ***EIF1AX*** (rank 8, $\mathrm{normZ} = -4.09$) alongside ***L3MBTL2*** (PRC1.6 subunit) and ***UBR5***. Comparing HT1080 and A549 establishes why different gametologs score across screens: parental HT1080 is unusually tolerant of *DDX3X* loss (`Chronos +0.18`) while *EIF1AX* and *RPS4X* guides deplete to the count floor before `D0` (`Supp Fig 4.7`, `Supp Fig 4.9`), whereas parental A549 already depends strongly on *DDX3X* (`Chronos -0.98`), leaving wider dynamic range for *EIF1AX*.
- **Multi-omic integration:** Integrating Chapter 3 RNA-seq, promoter ATAC-seq, and *UTY*/*KDM5D* rescue profiles proves that HT1080 candidate dependencies are **not** transcriptionally downregulated or promoter-closed at baseline ($\rho = -0.005$; `Supp Fig 4.11`), ruling out self-silencing and pointing to functional reliance on SAGA/Mediator coactivators.
- **27-screen external isogenic benchmark & technical QC audits:** Reprocessing 27 published isogenic CRISPR screens (Desjardins et al., 2026; Feng et al., 2022) shows that ***DDX3X* sensitization is unique to LOY (0/27 external contrasts)**, whereas SAGA subunit sensitization recurs in 13q arm-loss and *KEAP1*-mutant models (`Supp Fig 4.15`). Technical audits identify systematic non-detection of Brunello guides with `TCTC`/`AGACG` 5′ prefixes and recurring PCR-jackpotted guides shared between HT1080 `D0` and A549 `P3` ($\rho = 0.997$; `Supp Fig 4.6`), and show across 29 screens that baseline `T0`/`D0` divergence predicts when `IsogenicZ` and `drugZ` rankings diverge ($\rho = 0.61$; `Supp Fig 4.16`).

## §7 Reciprocal Two-Colour Spectral Flow Competition Assays (`07_competitive_growth_assays/`)

- **Thesis section:** Chapter 4, §4.3.2–4.3.4 (`Fig 4.5–4.6`, `Supp Fig 4.12`).
- **Assay calibration & baseline co-culture fitness:** Reciprocal `eGFP`/`mCherry` co-cultures of HT1080 `sgCTRL` and `LOY` cells quantified on the `BD FACSDiscover A8` spectral flow cytometer with explicit autofluorescence unmixing achieve near-unity linearity across 9-point mixing series ($R^2 > 0.996$; `Fig 4.5`). In unperturbed co-cultures, Y-depleted HT1080 cells display a modest baseline proliferative advantage over `sgCTRL` across both colour orientations.
- **Targeted knockout validation:** After Cas9 RNP knockout (verified by genomic PCR and ddPCR), interim `D0`-to-`D4` reciprocal log-odds shifts (`Fig 4.6`, `Supp Fig 4.12`) confirm selective fitness penalties in `LOY` relative to `sgCTRL` following ***DDX3X*** or ***TADA2B*** perturbation in both dye-swap orientations, whereas *SREBF1* shows smaller orientation-sensitive shifts at `D4`.
